t: You're looking at His Majesty's Theatre, on the Haymarket in the City of Westminster. It was built in 1897 for the actor-manager Herbert Beerbohm Tree, to a design by Charles J. Phipps, an architect who designed more than forty theatres in the later nineteenth century. Tree founded the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art here and staged spectacular Shakespeare. Premieres by Bernard Shaw and J. M. Synge followed, and later Noël Coward and J. B. Priestley. The wide stage suits big musicals, and the theatre has hosted record runs, including Chu Chin Chow and The Phantom of the Opera.
